title: Beja
intro: Beja is a city in Portugal with a population of 36,000 people (2011). It stands on the summit of a high hill surrounded by beautiful and fertile valleys under cultivation, as the district is rich in agricultural products, mainly cereals, olive oil, and wine.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html: Beja is a city in Portugal with a population of 36,000 people (2011). It stands on the summit of a high hill surrounded by beautiful and fertile valleys under cultivation, as the district is rich in agricultural products, mainly cereals, olive oil, and wine.

sections.title: Understand
sections.html:
The municipality of Beja (BEH-zhuh or BAY-zhuh, /ˈbɛ.ʒɐ/ or /ˈbɐj.ʒɐ/) is composed of 18 parishes and is the capital of the District of Beja.

The city is supposed to be the Roman Pax Julia, or Paca, and is still surrounded by remains of old Roman walls, which however, were partly restored during the Middle Ages. Beja was taken from the Moors in 1162 by Afonso Henriques.

Its castle, built by King Dom Diniz, is believed to be the best example of medieval architecture still extant in Portugal. It is a square, massive structure 36.5 m (120 feet) high, from the top of which the whole of the Alentejo country and the Cintra mountains may be seen. The walls of the castle are covered with hieroglyphics.

It was in its early days an episcopal city, but at the time of the invasion by the Moors, it lost its dignity. The Cathedral of Beja is an old temple, though so much modernized as to make it impossible to determine with any degree of certainty its original date.

Other famous churches are those of Our Lady of the Conception, St. Iago, or Santiago, and Santa Maria da Feira, said to have been an old Moorish mosque. The College of St. Sissenando, which belonged to the Jesuits, and was built principally at the expense of Donna Maria Sophia, in 1695, stands in the street where the saint was born. Part of this building is now occupied by the episcopal palace.

The city has modern improvements, schools, banks, libraries, etc. It is said to be the richest in Roman remains of all the cities in Portugal, except Évora, which now possesses a large collection of Roman antiquities collected in Beja.

sections.title: See
sections.html:
• Beja Castle, ☏ +351 284 311 913, turismo@cm-beja.pt. 9:30-12:30 14:00-18:00 (Closes: 01 Jan, 25 Apr, 01 May, 25 Dec). A medieval castle with a tower, fortifications, and landscaped gardens. 2€ / 1€ (Tower / Interpretative route of the castle). 
  • Convent of Our Lady of Conceição and Queen D.Leonor Regional Museum (Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Conceição e Museu Rainha Dona Leonor), ☏ +371 284 323 351. The city museum is housed in the former Convent of Beja. The convent was founded in 1495. The museum has a very surprising collection of ancient art, among other things. (updated Feb 2021)
  • Ovibeja. Agriculture, livestock, handicraft and tourism fair/expo. 
  • Casa das Artes - Jorge Vieira Museum, Largo Dr. Lima Faleiro, ☏ +351 284 311 920, museujorgevieira@cm-beja.pt. Tue-Sun 9:30-12:30 14:00-17:30 (Closes: Mon, 1 Jan, 25 Apr, 1 May, 25 Dec). Jorge Vieira's sculptures in a permanent collection. Free. 
  • Botanic Museum.  
  • Villa Romana de Pisões (Roman Villa of Pisões), ☏ +351 266 769 450. Tue–Sun 09:00–17:00, closed Mon.  
  • Beja Municipal Library - José Saramago, bibliotecamunicipaldebeja@cm-beja.pt.  
  • Casa da Cultura (Culture house).  
  • Teatro Municipal Theatre - Pax Julia, ☏ +351 284 315 090.  
  • Escudeiros Gallery.  
  • Beja Pillory
  • Santo Amaro Church.  
  • Santo André Chapel
  • Mercy Church
  • Holly Mary of Fair Church
  • Bullfight Square
  • Núcleo Museológico da Rua do Sembrano (Archaeological museum), Rua do Sembrano/Largo de S. João, ☏ +351 964934162, museusembrano@cm-beja.pt. Tue-Sun 09:30-12:30 14:00-18:00 (Closes: Mon, 1 Jan, 25 Apr, 1 May, 25 Dec). Includes a set of archaeological structures that provide a glimpse into some moments in the city's history and how the area evolved.
    The oldest remains, some ceramic fragments, point to occupation of this site dating back to the 3rd millennium BC.     Free. (updated Aug 2025)
  • Igreja de Santo Amaro (Nucleo visigótico do Museu Regional de Beja), Largo de Santo Amaro, 7800 Beja, ☏ 284 323 351Country code missing, museuregionaldebeja@cultura-alentejo.gov.pt. Tue-Sun 10:00-12:30 14:00-17:30 (Closes: Mon, 1 Jan, 25 Apr, 1 May, 25 Dec). One of the oldest churches in the city of Beja, it hosts a museum project that is part of an important collection from the Visigothic period. The Church of Santo Amaro is one of the oldest in the city of Beja, pointing many authors to a paleochristian foundation of this temple; more recent studies point to a dating from the tenth century, in the middle of the Islamic era, built by the Mozarabic community of Beja. The church underwent successive renovations over time, which gave rise to the current building, from the fifteenth/sixteenth centuries. In the 90s of the last century, the monument hosted a museum project related to the Visigothic era. It is considered, by some authors, as the most significant collection of the Visigothic period in Portugal Free (Temporarily due to renovation of the Museu Regional de Beja). (updated Oct 2026)

sections.title: Eat
sections.html:
• Restaurante Dom Dinis, Rua Dom Dinis 11, ☏ +351 284 324 142. Thu–Sun 12:00–15:00 & 19:30–22:00, Tue 12:00–15:00, closed Wed. €10-22. (updated Jun 2021)
  • Restaurante Íntimo, Rua dos Açores 12, ☏ +351 284 329 102. Thu–Sun 10:00–23:00, closed Mon. Mid-range. (updated Jun 2021)
  • Sabores do Monte, Monte da Juliana, Santa Vitória, ☏ +351 284 070 378, sergiojrbravo@gmail.com. Daily 09:00–22:30. Regional cooking, grilled meats and sausages. Mid-range. (updated Jun 2021)

sections.title: Mid-range
sections.html: • Vila Galé Clube de Campo, Herdade da Figueirinha, Santa Vitória, ☏ +351 284 970 100, campo@vilagale.com. 25 km (16 mi) from Beja, has 78 bedrooms, 3 junior suites and gives you access to a range of entertainment activities, mini-golf, hiking, four-wheel motorcycle or bicycle riding, water sports (paddle boating and sailing), duck shooting, and Portuguese bull-tackling bravado in the riding stable or arena. Booking online.

sections.title: Splurge
sections.html:
• Pousada Convento Beja, Largo D. Nuno Álvares Pereira, ☏ +351 284 313 580, fax: +351 284 329 143, recepcao.sfrancisco@pousadas.pt. In the 13th-century Franciscan Convent the historical centre of Beja is a luxury hotel. 
  • Herdade da Malhadinha Nova, Albernoa, ☏ +351 284 965 432, reservas@malhadinhanova.pt. Check-in: 14:00, check-out: 12:00. Five-star, 6-unit country-house hotel with two swimming pools, sauna, bar, free breakfast, free Wi-Fi, and free parking. €274-826. (updated Jul 2021)
